_comment: Providers the gateway serves, in fallback order for model "auto". Golden rule: free and keyless. A copy at <state dir>/providers.json (default ~/.ai-gateway/providers.json) replaces this built-in list, so a broken provider is a config edit, not a rebuild. kind openai: an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (url, optional models_url). kind cli: a vendor CLI run headless (bin, ask_args with {prompt}, optional model_args with {model}). kind tty: an interactive terminal app with no prompt flag, driven through a pseudo-terminal (bin, args; see the tty fields in internal/provider/provider.go). default_model empty = the first model the provider lists. min_interval_seconds spaces calls out; daily_limit 0 = no cap known. A CLI runs in an empty scratch directory with the entry's env added. disabled: true keeps an entry in the file without serving it.

providers.note: Only opencode's own free hosted models are listed. A model is always passed, because opencode's default on betelgeuse is the local bill-the-cat. Its google/* models use an API key, so the golden rule excludes them.

Freebuff has no prompt flag, so it is driven through a pseudo-terminal. The screen tells when the reply is finished (freebuff 0.2.36 layout: the typed prompt ends with a copy mark, and a finished reply is followed by a line with the copy mark and its duration). The reply itself is read from the conversation file freebuff saves, which is then deleted; the screen is the fallback, and there a reply longer than the screen is an error, not cut short. Freebuff's own banner says it may use data for AI training.
